summary:
During long-duration exploration missions to the Moon and Mars, communication latencies make real-time telemedicine from Earth mission control challenging. Crews  must rely on onboard autonomous intelligence to manage acute and chronic medical risks.


AEROS (Autonomous Exomedical Response & Onboard System) is an autonomous clinical copilot and health surveillance engine engineered for deep-space missions. Built on physiological telemetry modeled after the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Bio-Monitor smart shirt, AEROS operates across two synchronized operational horizons:


- Micro-Horizon (1Hz Real-Time EVA): Multi-radar physiological monitoring (ECG, SpO2, dual-band respiration) combined with spacesuit comms acoustic voice biomarker analysis to detect acute exertional hypoxia and autonomic uncoupling outside the airlock.


- Macro-Horizon (30-Day Medical Bay): Longitudinal habitability surveillance tracking cumulative sleep debt, vagal cardiac strain, interactive body-map localization, and crew self-reports.


AEROS enforces a strict zero-hallucination clinical decision contract: all triage recommendations are directly grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) evidence protocols and flight rules, providing crew safety when Earth is out of reach.
details:
AEROS

Autonomous Exomedical Response & Onboard Sentinel

An autonomous clinical copilot and health surveillance platform engineered for deep-space missions where communication delays (up to 22 minutes each way to Mars) render synchronous telemedicine from Earth difficult or impossible.

AEROS operates across two synchronized operational horizons

Micro-Horizon (1Hz Real-Time EVA Crisis)

Monitors high-frequency wearable telemetry (3-lead ECG, forehead pulse oximetry SpO₂, dual-band respiratory inductance plethysmography, blood pressure pulse transit time, and 3-axis accelerometer METs). AEROS fuses these vitals with acoustic vocal biomarker analysis from spacesuit comms (tracking jitter, pitch instability, and vocal strain) to instantly detect acute exertional hypoxia and autonomic uncoupling during spacewalks, rendering emergency countermeasures directly onto an EVA Helmet Visor HUD.

Macro-Horizon (30-Day Longitudinal Medical Bay)

Tracks cumulative multi-week physiological trends aboard the habitat—quantifying chronic sleep debt, vagal cardiac deconditioning, and circadian disruption against an astronaut’s individualized pre-flight baseline (L - 30). It features an interactive anatomical body map and a daily self-assessment check-in tool that re-scores clinical status live in the browser.

AEROS enforces a strict zero-hallucination clinical contract

Triage recommendations are mapped deterministically to official NASA Human Research Program (HRP) evidence reports. If clinical data is ambiguous or no approved protocol exists, AEROS explicitly declares an unknown state and safely escalates, refusing to generate speculative medical advice.

AEROS Benefits

Autonomous Survival: Provides immediate clinical decision support without waiting for ground control.

Objective-Subjective Cross-Checking

Automatically cross-references wearable sensor data against astronaut self-reports (e.g., flagging an astronaut who reports feeling "fine" when heart rate variability shows severe autonomic exhaustion, or catching early subjective symptoms before sensor drift).

Dual-Perspective Interface

Designed both for the high-stress, hands-free tactical environment of an astronaut on EVA and for the deep diagnostic review of an onboard Medical Officer or Earth Flight Surgeon.

Deterministic Patient Safety

Decouples safety-critical anomaly gating from generative AI, ensuring 100% auditable and medically defensible interventions.

Project Impact

In Spaceflight

Enables long-duration human exploration missions—such as Artemis lunar base camp stays and crewed transits to Mars—by mitigating the risks of medical contingencies in deep space (NASA Hazard: Distance from Earth).

On Earth (Terrestrial Spin-off)

Serves as an open-source autonomous health sentinel for extreme and remote environments where physicians are unavailable—including Antarctic research stations, offshore maritime platforms, submarine deployments, combat search-and-rescue, and isolated rural telemedicine clinics.

Technical stack

Languages & Architecture

Python 3.12 (pure hexagonal architecture core, clinical decision engine, and synthetic vitals generator) and JavaScript (reactive web console with a hand-ported in-browser scoring engine, kept in parity with the Python core via automated tests).

UI & Audio Engineering

HTML5 Canvas 2D (60fps continuous physiological waveforms, sparklines, and 4-domain multi-radars), Web Audio API (real-time 380Hz–3.2kHz spacesuit bandpass filtering and dynamic vocal synthesis), and CSS Grid/Flexbox for aerospace-grade responsive displays.

Hardware & Sensor Heritage

Modeled directly after the flight-proven sensor suite of the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Bio-Monitor (Astroskin smart shirt) deployed aboard the International Space Station, coupled with NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures baseline protocols.

Testing & Tooling

Automated test suites via pytest (74/74 domain and contract tests) and Node.js test runners ensuring mathematical parity between the Python telemetry core and browser client.

Creative considerations

Rather than presenting a generic vitals dashboard, AEROS creates a cinematic and clinically rigorous dual-view experience:

Acoustic Voice Biomarker Integration listens to how astronauts speak over spacesuit radio—detecting subtle acoustic tremor and fatigue signatures that precede physical collapse, exactly as a seasoned flight surgeon would.

Tactical Helmet HUD visualisations transforms telemetry into a heads-up visor display that cuts through cognitive overload during an emergency, shifting from diagnostic graphs to direct actionable directives (ACTION: ENGAGE O2 PURGE • RETURN TO AIRLOCK).

The interactive Anatomical Symptom Mapping connects self-reported discomfort with physiological sensor regions on a clickable 2D/3D body silhouette.

Other considerations

Human Factors & Dark Adaptation

Implemented a matte aerospace palette to reduce eye fatigue and prevent optical glare in dark spacecraft environments. Color is strictly reserved for clinical semantics (green, amber, red indicate triage priority and nothing else).

Cognitive Load in Emergencies

During high-stress EVAs, dense numbers and complex charts are automatically suppressed in favor of high-contrast status radars and singular action verbs.

Edge Resilience

Built as a lightweight, zero-dependency edge application that executes entirely client-side without requiring internet connectivity or cloud servers.
